html:
Riots in Accra that began on 28 February 1948, when police fired on a march of former soldiers taking a petition to the governor at Christiansborg, killing three of them.

The veterans had fought for Britain in the Second World War and were angry at unpaid benefits; townspeople were also boycotting high import prices. Looting of European and Syrian shops followed, and dozens died in days of riots. The British arrested the Big Six leaders of the United Gold Coast Convention, among them Kwame Nkrumah. An inquiry blamed the colonial system, and new constitutions followed. In 1949 Nkrumah founded the Convention People's Party and led the colony to independence.
sum: Riots in Accra that began on 28 February 1948, when police fired on a march of former soldiers taking a petition to the governor at Christiansborg, killing three of them.
